title: Perplexity API Platform overview
body:
# Overview

> Perplexity API Platform - build with the Orchestrator, Agent, Search, Embeddings, and Decisions APIs. Real-time, web-wide research and Q&A capabilities for your products.

The Perplexity API Platform is five APIs that share one API key and one host, `api.perplexity.ai`. Each does a different job and has its own endpoint (Orchestrator uses the base URL `https://api.perplexity.ai/orchestrator/v1`). Pick by what you need back:

| You need | Use | What you get back |
| - | - | - |
| Web sources for a model or agent you already run | [Search API](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search/quickstart.md) | Ranked web results as JSON: `title`, `url`, `date`, and page text extracted into `snippet`. No model, no generated answer, billed per request. |
| A hosted model that searches, reasons, and uses tools for you | [Agent API](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/quickstart.md) | A finished answer with citations from models by OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, and others, with `web_search`, `fetch_url`, `sandbox`, and your own tools. |
| A classification or a probability, not prose | [Decisions API](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/decisions/quickstart.md) | Calibrated probabilities for yes/no, multiple-choice, and rubric questions about text, JSON, or images. Models: `pplx-decider-v1.2` and `pplx-decider-flash-v1.2`. |
| Direct model calls in the OpenAI or Anthropic request format | [Orchestrator API](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/orchestrator/quickstart.md) (private preview) | Chat Completions, Responses, or Messages responses from any model in the catalog, routed to a healthy deployment. |
| Vectors for semantic search, retrieval, or RAG | [Embeddings API](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/embeddings/quickstart.md) | Embedding vectors from `pplx-embed-v1-0.6b`, `pplx-embed-v1-4b`, and the contextualized `pplx-embed-context-v1-0.6b` and `pplx-embed-context-v1-4b`. |

To make your first call, follow the [Quickstart](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/quickstart.md). Get an API key from the [API console](https://console.perplexity.ai). For the rates and billing rules of every API, see [Pricing](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/pricing.md).

title: Quickstart (getting started)
body:
# Quickstart

> Generate an API key and make your first call in < 3 minutes.

## Generating an API Key

> [card] [Get your Perplexity API Key](https://console.perplexity.ai/project/keys)
>
> Generate a new key on the **API Keys** page in the API Console.

> [!NOTE]
>
> See the [Projects](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/projects.md) page to learn more about projects.

> [card] [Pricing](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/pricing.md)
>
> Pay-as-you-go pricing for all APIs. No subscription required.

## Overview

The Perplexity API provides five core APIs for different use cases: the **Orchestrator API**, **Agent API**, **Search API**, **Embeddings API**, and **Decisions API**.

## Available APIs

> [card] [Orchestrator API](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/orchestrator/quickstart.md)
>
> Unified access to open-weight models hosted by Perplexity through OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoints.

> [card] [Agent API](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/quickstart.md)
>
> Get web-grounded answers with built-in citations in one call, or access third-party models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and xAI with web search tools and effort levels.

> [card] [Search API](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search/quickstart.md)
>
> Get raw, ranked web search results with advanced filtering and real-time data.

> [card] [Embeddings API](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/embeddings/quickstart.md)
>
> Generate high-quality embeddings for semantic search and RAG pipelines.

> [card] [Decisions API](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/decisions/quickstart.md)
>
> Get typed answers with probabilities for yes/no, multiple-choice, and rubric questions about text and images.

## Choosing the Right API

> [accordion] Use the Orchestrator API when...
>
> * You want **one API for open-weight models** hosted by Perplexity, with a single API key
> * You have **existing OpenAI or Anthropic SDK code**: switching is a base URL and API key change
> * You want **routing and failover across model deployments** handled for you instead of building it yourself
>
> **Best for:** Model-agnostic products, multi-model workloads, drop-in replacement for OpenAI or Anthropic SDK integrations

> [accordion] Use the Agent API when...
>
> * You want **web-grounded answers with built-in citations** - send a message and get a researched, cited response, with conversation context when you need it
> * You prefer **simplicity**: pick a [effort level](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/effort.md) and get a researched answer in one call, or take **granular control** over model, reasoning, token budgets, and tools
> * You need **multi-provider access** to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, and Perplexity's own model through one API
>
> **Best for:** AI assistants, research and Q\&A tools, agentic workflows, custom AI applications

> [accordion] Use the Search API when...
>
> * You need **raw search results** without LLM processing
> * You want to **build custom AI workflows** with your own models
> * You need **search data** for indexing, analysis, or training
>
> **Best for:** Custom AI pipelines, data collection, search integration

> [accordion] Use the Embeddings API when...
>
> * You need **semantic similarity** between texts for search or recommendations
> * You're building **RAG pipelines** that require vector representations of documents
> * You need to **cluster, classify, or compare** text without generating a response
>
> **Best for:** Semantic search, RAG applications, text classification, recommendation systems

> [accordion] Use the Decisions API when...
>
> * You need a **yes/no answer, one of your options, or a level on your rubric** instead of generated text
> * You want **probabilities you can threshold** in code, with no output parsing
> * You want to ask **many questions about the same content**, including images, in one request
>
> **Best for:** Classification, routing, grading against a rubric, filtering and gating decisions

## Installation

Install the SDK for your preferred language:

```bash Python theme={null}
pip install perplexityai
```

```bash Typescript theme={null}
npm install @perplexity-ai/perplexity_ai
```

## Authentication

Set your API key as an environment variable:

> [tab] macOS/Linux
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> export PERPLEXITY_API_KEY="your_api_key_here"
> ```

> [tab] Windows
>
> ```powershell theme={null}
> setx PERPLEXITY_API_KEY "your_api_key_here"
> ```

Confirm the key is set without printing it:

> [tab] macOS/Linux
>
> ```bash theme={null} theme={null} theme={null}
> test -n "$PERPLEXITY_API_KEY" && echo "PERPLEXITY_API_KEY is set" || echo "PERPLEXITY_API_KEY is not set"
> ```

> [tab] Windows
>
> ```powershell theme={null} theme={null} theme={null}
> if ($env:PERPLEXITY_API_KEY) { "PERPLEXITY_API_KEY is set" } else { "PERPLEXITY_API_KEY is not set" }
> ```

> [!WARNING]
>
> Never print the key or any part of it. Commands like `env`, `echo $PERPLEXITY_API_KEY`, or a prefix or length check leave the key in shell history, logs, and coding-agent transcripts. Read the key from the environment in code and tests, and don't paste it into fixtures or commit messages.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **OpenAI SDK compatible:** The Agent API follows the OpenAI Responses API format. Point the OpenAI SDK at `https://api.perplexity.ai/v1` and call `client.responses.create()`; the canonical endpoint is `POST /v1/agent`, and `POST /v1/responses` is accepted as an alias. See the [OpenAI Compatibility Guide](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/openai-compatibility.md). For the OpenAI Chat Completions format, use the [Orchestrator API](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/orchestrator/quickstart.md) at `POST /orchestrator/v1/chat/completions`.

## Making Your First API Call

Choose your API based on your use case:

> [tab] Orchestrator API
>
> Use for direct access to open-weight models with the OpenAI SDK:
>
> ```python Python theme={null}
> from openai import OpenAI
> import os
>
> # Point the OpenAI SDK at the Orchestrator API base URL
> client = OpenAI(
>     api_key=os.environ.get("PERPLEXITY_API_KEY"),
>     base_url="https://api.perplexity.ai/orchestrator/v1"
> )
>
> # Make the API call with any model from the Orchestrator API catalog
> response = client.chat.completions.create(
>     model="perplexity/kimi-k3",
>     max_tokens=1024,
>     messages=[
>         {"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the key trade-offs between vector and keyword search."}
>     ]
> )
>
> print(response.choices[0].message.content)
> ```
>
> ```typescript TypeScript theme={null}
> import OpenAI from 'openai';
>
> // Point the OpenAI SDK at the Orchestrator API base URL
> const client = new OpenAI({
>     apiKey: process.env.PERPLEXITY_API_KEY,
>     baseURL: "https://api.perplexity.ai/orchestrator/v1"
> });
>
> // Make the API call with any model from the Orchestrator API catalog
> const response = await client.chat.completions.create({
>     model: "perplexity/kimi-k3",
>     max_tokens: 1024,
>     messages: [
>         { role: "user", content: "Summarize the key trade-offs between vector and keyword search." }
>     ]
> });
>
> console.log(response.choices[0].message.content);
> ```
>
> ```bash cURL theme={null}
> curl -X POST 'https://api.perplexity.ai/orchestrator/v1/chat/completions' \
>   -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERPLEXITY_API_KEY" \
>   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
>   -d '{
>     "model": "perplexity/kimi-k3",
>     "max_tokens": 1024,
>     "messages": [
>       {"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the key trade-offs between vector and keyword search."}
>     ]
>   }' | jq
> ```

>
> Use for typed answers with probabilities about your content. Call `client.decisions.create` with your content as `state`, a model, and named questions.
>
> ```python Python theme={null}
> from perplexity import Perplexity
>
> client = Perplexity(timeout=30.0)
>
> response = client.decisions.create(
>     model="pplx-decider-latest",
>     state={
>         "title": "Battery died after two weeks",
>         "review": "The headphones sound great, but the battery stopped charging after two weeks.",
>     },
>     questions={
>         "defect": {
>             "type": "noul",
>             "instructions": "Does the review report a product defect?",
>         },
>     },
> )
>
> print(response.answers["defect"].noul)  # probability of yes, 0 to 1
> ```

>   },
>   questions: {
>     defect: {
>       type: "noul",
>       instructions: "Does the review report a product defect?",
>     },
>   },
> });
> const { defect } = response.answers;
>
> if (defect?.type === "noul") console.log(defect.noul);  // probability of yes, 0 to 1
> ```

>       "defect": {
>         "type": "noul",
>         "instructions": "Does the review report a product defect?"
>       }
>     }
>   }'
> ```
>
> The response has one answer per question, under the name you gave it. A `noul` answer is the probability of yes, from 0 to 1. For `choice` and `score` questions, see the [Decisions API quickstart](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/decisions/quickstart.md).

>           "text": "The paper “Attention Is All You Need” introduced the **Transformer**, a sequence‑to‑sequence model built entirely from attention and feed‑forward layers, and showed it could beat recurrent and convolutional models on machine translation while training much faster and scaling better.[web:1][web:8] This architectural shift made self‑attention the default building block for modern NLP and enabled today’s large language models.[web:2][web:4][web:7]\n\n## Core technical ideas\n\n- The Transformer removes recurrence and convolutions, using stacked self‑attention and position‑wise feed‑forward layers in both encoder and decoder.[web:1][web:3] Positional encodings are added to token embeddings so the model can represent order despite having no recurrence.[web:1]  \n- It introduces **multi‑head** attention: several parallel attention heads project queries/keys/values, attend in different subspaces, then concatenate and linearly mix their outputs.[web:1][web:2] This lets the model capture different types of relations (e.g., syntax and coreference) in parallel.[web:1]  \n- The paper emphasizes three attention types within the architecture: encoder self‑attention, decoder masked self‑attention (preventing access to future tokens), and encoder‑decoder attention where the decoder attends over encoder outputs.[web:1][web:8]\n\n## Empirical results in the paper\n\n- On WMT 2014 English→German translation, the base Transformer reaches 28.4 BLEU, surpassing prior state of the art, including ensembles, by over 2 BLEU.[web:1][web:3] On WMT 2014 English→French, a single Transformer achieves 41.8 BLEU after 3.5 days of training on 8 GPUs, outperforming earlier, much more expensive systems.[web:1]  \n- The authors also show the model generalizes beyond translation by achieving strong results on English constituency parsing, even with limited labeled data.[web:1][web:9] These results demonstrate that attention‑only architectures are not just viable but competitive across sequence tasks.[web:1]\n\n## Why it was faster and more scalable\n\n- Self‑attention lets the model process all tokens in a sequence in parallel, unlike RNNs/LSTMs that must step through tokens sequentially, which makes it far more compatible with GPU/TPU hardware.[web:1][web:7] This parallelism reduced training time “by up to an order of magnitude” relative to recurrent models on the same tasks.[web:8]  \n- For typical sequence lengths, the attention‑based layers in the paper have lower or comparable per‑layer computational complexity than recurrent or convolutional alternatives and much shorter paths between distant tokens, which helps learn long‑range dependencies.[web:1][web:6] This combination of efficiency and representational power is what made large‑scale pretraining feasible.[web:7][web:10]\n\n## How it changed NLP\n\n- The Transformer architecture became the foundation for major pretrained models such as BERT (encoder‑only), GPT (decoder‑only), and many others, which now dominate benchmarks in translation, question answering, summarization, and general language modeling.[web:2][web:7][web:10] These models exploit the same self‑attention blocks introduced in the 2017 paper, often with minor variants.[web:2]  \n- By showing that attention‑only, highly parallel architectures can outperform traditional sequence models, the paper shifted the field’s default design pattern from RNNs/CNNs to transformers and opened the path to scaling parameters and data to today’s very large language models.[web:2][web:4][web:7] Its influence now extends beyond NLP to vision, speech, and multimodal models that reuse the same core transformer building blocks.[web:2][web:4]",

body:
# Pricing

> Understand Perplexity API pricing, model rates, request fees, billing setup, and rate-limit references.

Each Perplexity API bills differently. The rates are in the sections below.

* **Orchestrator API:** per token, at each model's rates. No per-request fees. Requests rejected with a `429` are not billed.
* **Agent API:** per token, at each model's rates, plus tool fees. Most tools bill per call; `sandbox` bills per session, plus each SDK search query made inside it. The `flex` (0.5×) and `priority` (2×) service tiers change the token rates only for models that list that tier on the [Agent API Models page](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/models.md). Other models always bill at the listed rate.
* **Search API:** per successful request.
* **Embeddings API:** per token.
* **Decisions API:** per input token. Output tokens are free. With `mode: "web_grounding"`, each web search adds \$0.001.

For billing setup, payment methods, and usage monitoring, see the [Admin section](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/projects.md). For rate limits, see [Rate Limits & Usage Tiers](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/admin/rate-limits-usage-tiers.md).

## Orchestrator API Pricing

Orchestrator API usage is billed per token at each model's published rates — there are no per-request fees. Every model has its own input and output rate, with cache reads billed at the model's discounted cache-read rate and reasoning tokens billed at the output rate. You are always billed at the requested model's rates, regardless of how the request is served.

See [Orchestrator Models & Pricing](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/orchestrator/models.md) for the full per-model rate card, including cache-read rates.

## Agent API Pricing

The Agent API provides access to third-party models from providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, Z.AI, Moonshot AI, and NVIDIA with **transparent, token-based pricing** at each model's published rates.

### Model Pricing

Agent API pricing varies by provider and model, with each provider offering multiple models at different price points.

The input, output, and cache-read rate for each model is on the [Agent API Models page](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/models.md).

### Tool Pricing

When using tools with the Agent API:

| Tool | Price | Description |
| - | :-: | - |
| **`web_search` (standard)** | \$0.0025 per invocation | Standard web search with `search_type: "web"`. \$2.50 per 1,000 invocations |
| **`web_search` (Fast Search)** | \$0.001 per invocation | The same tool with `search_type: "fast"`. \$1.00 per 1,000 invocations. See [Fast Search](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search/fast-search.md) |
| **`image_search`** | \$0.0025 per successful invocation | Finds structured image results with domain, format, and safe-search filters. \$2.50 per 1,000 successful invocations |
| **`fetch_url`** | \$0.0005 per invocation | Fetches and extracts content from specific URLs |
| **`people_search`** | \$0.005 per invocation | Looks up professionals, employees, and people. \$5 per 1,000 tool invocations |
| **`finance_search`** | \$0.005 per invocation | Retrieves financial data and market information. \$5 per 1,000 tool invocations |
| **`sandbox`** | \$0.03 per session | Isolated container for executing code during an Agent API request. A session covers up to 20 minutes of active use for billing purposes — this is the billing window, not a runtime cap. SDK search queries made from inside the sandbox are billed at \$0.0025 per request (same as `web_search`). |

> [!NOTE]
>
> Most tool costs are per invocation. `sandbox` is billed per container session — a 20-minute billing window per container, not a runtime cap — plus per SDK search query made from inside it. Tool costs are separate from model token costs.

## Search API Pricing

| API | Price per 1K requests | Description |
| - | :-: | - |
| **Search API** | \$5.00 | Ranked web results as JSON, with page text extracted into each result's `snippet`. No model, no generated answer, no token billing. Filter by domain, language, and date, and bias results by country. |
| **Search API with [Fast Search](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search/fast-search.md)** | \$1.00 | Lower-latency results in the same response format. Set `search_type: "fast"` |

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Billing unit:** Search API charges for each successful `POST /search` request, not for each query in the request. A successful request containing an array of up to five queries is one billing unit. Invalid requests, rate-limited requests, and upstream failures are not billed. A successful response is billed even when it returns no results. There are no additional token-based charges.

Search API cost = successful requests ÷ 1,000 × the price per 1K requests. The amount of extracted text (`max_tokens`, `max_tokens_per_page`) does not change the price.

| Request | Billing units | Cost |
| - | :-: | -: |
| One `POST /search` with one query, up to 20 results | 1 | \$5.00 ÷ 1,000 = \$0.005 |
| One `POST /search` with one query and `search_type: "fast"` | 1 | \$1.00 ÷ 1,000 = \$0.001 |
| One `POST /search` with a `query` array of five queries | 1 | \$0.005 (standard) or \$0.001 (Fast Search) |
| 10,000 successful standard requests in a month | 10,000 | 10 × \$5.00 = \$50.00 |

What a result contains, the request controls, and the limits on queries, results, and extracted text are in the [Search API overview](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search/overview.md).

## Embeddings API Pricing

Generate high-quality text embeddings for semantic search, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and other machine learning applications.

### Standard Embeddings

| Model | Dimensions | Price (\$/1M tokens) |
| - | :-: | :-: |
| `pplx-embed-v1-0.6b` | 1024 | \$0.004 |
| `pplx-embed-v1-4b` | 2560 | \$0.03 |

### Contextualized Embeddings

| Model | Dimensions | Price (\$/1M tokens) |
| - | :-: | :-: |
| `pplx-embed-context-v1-0.6b` | 1024 | \$0.008 |
| `pplx-embed-context-v1-4b` | 2560 | \$0.05 |

Embeddings cost = tokens ÷ 1,000,000 × the model's rate. For example, 40M tokens on `pplx-embed-context-v1-4b` cost 40 × \$0.05 = \$2.00.

To use the Embeddings API, see the [Embeddings quickstart](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/embeddings/quickstart.md).

## Decisions API Pricing

The Decisions API answers yes/no, multiple-choice, and scored questions about text and images with calibrated probabilities.

| Model | Price (\$/1M input tokens) | Output tokens | Per-request fee |
| - | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| `pplx-decider-v1.2` | \$0.02 | Free | None |
| `pplx-decider-flash-v1.2` | \$0.01 | Free | None |

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Aliases:** `pplx-decider-latest` and `perplexity/pplx-decider-latest` select `pplx-decider-v1.2`. `pplx-decider-flash-latest` and `perplexity/pplx-decider-flash-latest` select `pplx-decider-flash-v1.2`. An alias bills at the rate of the model it selects. Requests that name `pplx-decider-v1.1-27b` or `pplx-decider-v1-27b` select `pplx-decider-v1.2` and bill at \$0.02.
>
> **Billing unit:** you pay for input tokens, plus web searches and URL fetches if you set `mode: "web_grounding"`. The `state`, every question, any images, fetched page text, and any search results added to the `state` count as input; the response reports the exact number as `usage.input_tokens`, so you can compute the token cost of a request from the response you already receive. A request with 600 input tokens costs \$0.000012 on `pplx-decider-v1.2` and \$0.000006 on `pplx-decider-flash-v1.2`.

### Web grounding

A request with `mode: "web_grounding"` runs one [Fast Search](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search/fast-search.md) for each of its questions, up to 100, before the model answers. Each search costs \$0.001 (\$1 per 1,000), in addition to input tokens, so at most \$0.10 in searches per request. Questions that produce the same search query share one search.

When `state` is a page URL, the API also fetches the page before searching. Each successful URL fetch costs \$0.001; a failed fetch is not billed. One successful fetch and three successful searches cost \$0.004, plus input tokens.

* **Billed:** every search that returns, even with no results. Completed searches and successful URL fetches remain billable if the request later fails, for example because the input exceeds the token limit.
* **Not billed:** a search that fails or runs out of time, a question with no text to search, and requests rejected before search: an invalid `mode`, more than 100 questions, a missing or unknown `model`, or a `state` that is not a string, object, or array. A request can be billed for fewer searches than it has questions.
* **Input tokens:** fetched page text and search evidence are billed as input tokens and included in `usage.input_tokens`.

See [Web grounding](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/decisions/quickstart.md#web-grounding).

To use the Decisions API, see the [Decisions quickstart](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/decisions/quickstart.md).

Token counts: 1 token is about 4 characters of English text. The exact count varies with language and content.

## Cost Examples

To estimate an Agent API request, add these parts:

* uncached input tokens × the model's input rate ÷ 1,000,000
* cached input tokens × the model's cache-read rate ÷ 1,000,000
* output tokens × the model's output rate ÷ 1,000,000. The response reports reasoning tokens in `usage.output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`; the Models page notes where they bill at the output rate.
* the price of each tool call (from the Tool Pricing table)
* \$0.03 per `sandbox` session, plus \$0.0025 per SDK search query made inside it

Model rates are per 1M tokens, on the [Agent API Models page](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/models.md). Where a rate lists a context-length range, use the rate that matches the request's input size. With `flex` or `priority` on a model that lists that tier, multiply the token cost by 0.5 or 2. Tool fees don't change.

Actual effort level costs vary with the selected model, token usage, and tool invocations. When present on a completed response, `usage.cost.total_cost` reports the calculated request cost.

## Purchase Options

* [Perplexity API Platform on AWS Marketplace](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/resources/aws-marketplace.md): buy API credits through AWS Marketplace with consolidated billing and enterprise procurement.
* [Contact the sales team](https://perplexity.typeform.com/to/m3WnMaG6): ask about custom pricing, dedicated support, and enterprise features.

title: Orchestrator routing & reliability
body:
# Routing & Reliability

> How the Perplexity Orchestrator API routes requests across model deployments, and what happens automatically when a provider degrades or fails.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Orchestrator API is in private preview. Email [api@perplexity.ai](mailto:api@perplexity.ai) to request access.

## Overview

Depending on the model, a model id in the [catalog](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/orchestrator/models.md) can be served by any of several underlying deployments. The platform decides where each request runs — there are no routing parameters to set, and no per-provider configuration on your side. You send a model id; routing, health monitoring, and failover happen automatically.

Responses always echo the model id you requested, and billing always uses that model's [published rates](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/orchestrator/models.md), regardless of which deployment served the request.

## How Requests Are Routed

When a model has more than one deployment, traffic is spread across them according to a weighted split that is continuously adjusted based on observed health — error rates, capacity, and latency. Deployments that degrade shed traffic to healthy ones automatically and regain it gradually as they recover.

Multi-turn conversations are kept on the same deployment where possible, so prompt caching keeps working across requests — send the same conversation prefix and you benefit from [cache-read pricing](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/orchestrator/models.md) without doing anything special.

## Automatic Failover

When a deployment fails — a provider error, a rate limit, or a timeout — the request is retried on another deployment for that model when one is available. Each attempt is bounded by time-to-first-token and total-duration limits, and exceeding either counts as a failure.

Two behaviors worth designing around:

* **Errors you can fix are not retried.** Deterministic client errors — an invalid request or a prompt that exceeds the model's context window — surface immediately as a `400` rather than being retried across deployments.
* **When every deployment fails**, the request returns a `429` indicating the model is overloaded, with a `Retry-After` header. Retrying after the indicated interval is safe: requests that fail before producing any output are not billed.

## Streaming and Reliability

Failures before the first token are handled invisibly — failover happens before the stream starts, and you receive a normal response. If a stream fails after output has begun, it ends with an in-band error event; your client should treat an unterminated stream as incomplete. Streamed requests are billed for the tokens actually delivered.

## Next Steps

> [card] [Models & Pricing](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/orchestrator/models.md)
>
> The model catalog with per-token rates.

> [card] [API Reference](https://docs.perplexity.ai/api-reference/gateway-chat-completions-post.md)
>
> Request and response schemas, including error shapes.

title: Agent API quickstart
body:
# Agent API

> The Agent API is a multi-provider, interoperable API specification for building LLM applications. Access models from multiple providers with integrated real-time web search, tool configuration, reasoning control, and token budgets—all through one unified interface.

> [card] [Try the Agent API Playground](https://console.perplexity.ai/project/agent-playground)
>
> Test Agent API requests and parameters interactively in the API console.

> [card] [Pricing](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/pricing.md)
>
> Pay-as-you-go pricing for all APIs. No subscription required.

## Why Use the Agent API?

> [card] Web-Grounded Answers
>
> Get accurate, up-to-date answers grounded in real-time web search, with inline citations in a single call, and conversation context across turns.

> [card] Multi-Provider Access
>
> Access OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, and more through one unified API, no need to manage multiple API keys.

> [card] Transparent Pricing
>
> See exact token counts and published costs for every request.

> [card] Granular Control
>
> Change models, reasoning, tokens, and tools with consistent syntax.

> [!NOTE]
>
> We recommend using our [official SDKs](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/sdk/overview.md) for a more convenient and type-safe way to interact with the Agent API.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Endpoint:** The Agent API is available at `POST https://api.perplexity.ai/v1/agent`. For OpenAI SDK compatibility, `POST /v1/responses` is also accepted as an alias. See the [OpenAI Compatibility Guide](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/openai-compatibility.md) for details on using OpenAI SDKs with Perplexity.

## Installation

Install the SDK for your preferred language:

```bash Python theme={null}
pip install perplexityai
```

```bash Typescript theme={null}
npm install @perplexity-ai/perplexity_ai
```

## Authentication

Set your API key as an environment variable. The SDK will automatically read it:

> [tab] macOS/Linux
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> export PERPLEXITY_API_KEY="your_api_key_here"
> ```

> [tab] Windows
>
> ```powershell theme={null}
> setx PERPLEXITY_API_KEY "your_api_key_here"
> ```

Confirm the key is set without printing it:

> [tab] macOS/Linux
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> test -n "$PERPLEXITY_API_KEY" && echo "PERPLEXITY_API_KEY is set" || echo "PERPLEXITY_API_KEY is not set"
> ```

> [tab] Windows
>
> ```powershell theme={null}
> if ($env:PERPLEXITY_API_KEY) { "PERPLEXITY_API_KEY is set" } else { "PERPLEXITY_API_KEY is not set" }
> ```

> [!WARNING]
>
> Never print the key or any part of it. Commands like `env`, `echo $PERPLEXITY_API_KEY`, or a prefix or length check leave the key in shell history, logs, and coding-agent transcripts. Read the key from the environment in code and tests, and don't paste it into fixtures or commit messages.

> [!NOTE]
>
> All SDK examples below automatically use the `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY` environment variable. You can also pass the key explicitly if needed.

## Basic Usage

> [!TIP]
>
> **Convenience Property:** Both Python and Typescript SDKs provide an `output_text` property that aggregates all text content from response outputs. Instead of iterating through `response.output`, simply use `response.output_text` for cleaner code.
>
> Without an SDK, read the answer from the `output` array: take items with `"type": "message"`, then their `content` entries with `"type": "output_text"`. Agent API responses have no `choices[0].message.content`; that field belongs to the legacy Sonar Chat Completions format.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Web search is opt-in.** A request with only `model` and `input`, like the first example below, answers from the model's own knowledge and returns no citations. For web-grounded answers, add an `effort` or `tools: [{"type": "web_search"}]`. Both are shown further down this page.

### Using a Third-Party Model

Use third-party models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, and other providers for specific capabilities:

```python Python theme={null}
from perplexity import Perplexity

client = Perplexity()

response = client.responses.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.6-sol",
    input="Explain the difference between supervised and unsupervised learning in machine learning."
)

print(f"Response ID: {response.id}")
print(response.output_text)
```

```typescript Typescript theme={null}
import Perplexity from '@perplexity-ai/perplexity_ai';

const client = new Perplexity();

const response = await client.responses.create({
    model: "openai/gpt-5.6-sol",
    input: "Explain the difference between supervised and unsupervised learning in machine learning."
});

console.log(`Response ID: ${response.id}`);
console.log(response.output_text);
```

```bash cURL theme={null}
curl https://api.perplexity.ai/v1/agent \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERPLEXITY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "openai/gpt-5.6-sol",
```

# Agent API Models

> Compare Agent API models, token pricing, supported service tiers, and provider documentation.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Looking for ranked web results instead of a generated answer? Use the Search API at `POST /search`. It takes no `model` parameter and bills per successful request, not per token. Start with the [Search API quickstart](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search/quickstart.md).

## Available Models

The Agent API provides a unified interface to models from multiple providers with transparent token-based pricing.

Pricing rates are published per model and may differ from provider list prices. All charges are based on actual token consumption, and every API response includes exact token counts so you know your costs per request.

The **Service tiers** column lists optional non-default tiers. An em dash means the model uses default processing only.

A rate with a context-length range, such as `(≤272k)`, changes when the input is above that range. A single value applies at every context length.

## Service tiers

Omit `service_tier`, or set it to `auto` or `default`, to use default processing. `flex` uses lower-cost, best-effort capacity at 0.5× the listed token prices. `priority` uses higher-priority processing at 2× the listed token prices. `fast` is accepted as an alias for `priority`. These multipliers apply only to models that list the tier in the **Service tiers** column. Other models always bill at the listed rate.

When you provide `model` or `models`, the Agent API applies `flex` or `priority` only if the selected model—or every model in a fallback list—supports that tier. An unsupported tier does not cause the request to be rejected; the API ignores `service_tier` and uses default processing. Requests that specify only an effort level or profile retain the tier until the model is resolved. The response's `service_tier` field reports the tier that served the request.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Not all third-party models support all features (e.g., reasoning, tools). Check model documentation for specific capabilities.

title: Building agents: define the run
body:
# Define the run

> Configure the agent run: start from an effort level, then customize the system prompt, the loop bound, and the model.

Every agent run begins with one Agent API request. Before prompts, tools, or output format, you decide what runs and how far it can go. The fastest way to start is an `effort` — a tuned bundle of model, system prompt, search config, and tools — which you then customize with individual settings as needed. This page sets up the call the rest of this section builds on.

## Start from an effort level

A `effort` gives you a working agent in one field.

```python Python theme={null}
from perplexity import Perplexity

client = Perplexity()

response = client.responses.create(
    effort="low",
    input="Give me a thorough overview of the current state of solid-state battery commercialization.",
)

print(response.output_text)
```

```typescript TypeScript theme={null}
import Perplexity from '@perplexity-ai/perplexity_ai';

const client = new Perplexity();

const response = await client.responses.create({
  effort: 'low',
  input: 'Give me a thorough overview of the current state of solid-state battery commercialization.',
});

console.log(response.output_text);
```

```bash cURL theme={null}
curl https://api.perplexity.ai/v1/agent \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERPLEXITY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "effort": "low",
    "input": "Give me a thorough overview of the current state of solid-state battery commercialization."
  }' | jq
```

Other effort levels trade depth against latency and cost. See [Effort Levels](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/effort.md) for what each one bundles and how effort level updates are managed.

## Customize the system prompt: `instructions`

A `effort` ships its own tuned system prompt. The `instructions` field **is** the agent's system prompt — the standing rules that hold for every turn of the loop: role, tone, citation, and grounding rules. They apply regardless of what the user asks on a given turn.

```python theme={null}
instructions="You are a research assistant. Cite every claim by source domain, and never speculate beyond the retrieved evidence."
```

Setting `instructions` **replaces** the effort level's system prompt rather than appending to it. Omit `instructions` to keep the effort level's prompt.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Keep the system prompt lean. Every token here is re-processed on each step of the loop, so it adds up across tool calls. For machine-readable output or retrieval constraints, prefer request parameters (see [Structure the output](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/building-agents/shape-output.md) and [Give it tools](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/building-agents/give-it-tools.md)) over prose rules.

## Customize the loop: `max_steps`

An agent run is a loop: the model reasons, optionally calls tools, reads the results, and repeats until it answers. One step is one model turn plus the tool calls it makes in that turn. `max_steps` caps how many of these tool-calling turns a run may take. Use it to bound runaway loops and to trade latency against depth.

When a run uses all its steps and the last one called tools, the agent doesn't error. It makes one extra answer-only turn with tools disabled, and writes the final answer from the tool results it has gathered so far. If the model answers without calling a tool, the run ends there, before the cap.

At `max_steps: 1`, the agent gets one round of tool calls, then answers from their results. That is enough for a single search followed by an answer. It is not enough when the agent needs to act on what it found: search again, fetch a page from the results, or rerun code that failed. Tools that usually spend a step on setup get little or no work done: with `finance_search`, and with `sandbox` plus `web_search`, the agent typically loads the tool's instructions in its first step and only queries data or runs code after that.

When you specify `model` or `models` without an effort level, omitting `max_steps` defaults the run to 1 step. Set it explicitly whenever your tools need multiple turns. For direct-model requests that enable `finance_search`, use `max_steps: 3` or higher so the agent has enough room to initialize and run the tool. Effort levels provide their own step budget unless you override it.

```python theme={null}
response = client.responses.create(
    effort="low",
    input="Give me a thorough overview of the current state of solid-state battery commercialization.",
    max_steps=20,
)
```

If you pass `max_steps` alongside an `effort`, it overrides the effort level's value, up to the effort level's own ceiling for chat-style effort levels.

## Customize the model: `model` or `models`

An effort level picks a model for you. When you need full control over which model answers, set one explicitly instead of (or alongside) an effort level:

| Field | What it is |
| - | - |
| `model` | A single model in `provider/model` format, for example `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`. |
| `models` | A fallback chain of up to 5 models, tried in order until one succeeds. |

If you set `models`, it takes precedence over `model`. See [Models](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/models.md) for the catalog and pricing, and [Model fallback](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/model-fallback.md) for how the chain resolves.

> [!TIP]
>
> Start from an `effort`, then move to an explicit `model` (or `models` chain) when you need to pin the exact engine.

## Next steps

> [card] [Prompt the agent](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/building-agents/prompt-the-agent.md)
>
> Split the system prompt from the question, and ground the run.

> [card] [Effort Levels](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/effort.md)
>
> See the tuned effort levels you can start from.

title: Building agents: prompt the agent
body:
# Prompt the agent

> Split the standing rules (the system prompt) from the question (input), and ground the run so the agent searches and answers on the right thing.

An agent has two prompt surfaces, and keeping them distinct matters. `instructions` is the agent's **system prompt** — the rules that hold on every turn. `input` is the specific thing to do this turn. When retrieval tools are enabled, `input` is also what the model uses to decide whether and what to search. This page draws the line between the two and shows how to ground the run on retrieved evidence.

## `instructions` vs `input`

| Field | What goes here |
| - | - |
| `instructions` | The system prompt: role, tone, output language, citation and formatting rules, and hard do/don'ts. Applied on every turn of the loop, independent of the question. |
| `input` | The question or task for this turn. It guides tool selection, and when retrieval is enabled, it is what the model searches on, so a more specific `input` produces more targeted retrieval. |

A useful principle: if a rule should still apply when the user asks something completely different, it belongs in `instructions` (the system prompt). If it is about this request, it belongs in `input`.

```python Python theme={null}
from perplexity import Perplexity

client = Perplexity()

response = client.responses.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.6-sol",
    instructions=(
        "You are a financial analyst. Always cite sources by domain, "
        "and never speculate beyond retrieved evidence."
    ),
    input="Which operating segments did Apple report in its most recent annual 10-K, and how did each contribute to revenue?",
    tools=[{"type": "web_search"}],
)

print(response.output_text)
```

```typescript TypeScript theme={null}
import Perplexity from '@perplexity-ai/perplexity_ai';

const client = new Perplexity();

const response = await client.responses.create({
  model: 'openai/gpt-5.6-sol',
  instructions:
    'You are a financial analyst. Always cite sources by domain, and never speculate beyond retrieved evidence.',
  input: 'Which operating segments did Apple report in its most recent annual 10-K, and how did each contribute to revenue?',
  tools: [{ type: 'web_search' as const }],
});

console.log(response.output_text);
```

```bash cURL theme={null}
curl https://api.perplexity.ai/v1/agent \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERPLEXITY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "openai/gpt-5.6-sol",
    "instructions": "You are a financial analyst. Always cite sources by domain, and never speculate beyond retrieved evidence.",
    "input": "Which operating segments did Apple report in its most recent annual 10-K, and how did each contribute to revenue?",
    "tools": [{ "type": "web_search" }]
  }' | jq
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> With an `effort`, `instructions` replaces the effort level's tuned system prompt instead of appending to it. Omit `instructions` to keep the effort level prompt. See [Define the run](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/building-agents/define-the-run.md#customize-the-system-prompt-instructions).

## Ground the run

Grounding keeps the agent answering from retrieved evidence rather than from the model's own priors. Two levers do most of the work:

* Specific `input`. When retrieval tools are enabled, the model searches based on `input`. "Apple FY2025 10-K revenue by operating segment" retrieves more targeted results than "how is Apple doing." Name entities, time ranges, and the unit of the answer.
* Retrieval tools. Enable `web_search` and related tools so the agent pulls live evidence. See [Give it tools](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/building-agents/give-it-tools.md).

For hard constraints — allowed domains, date ranges, region — prefer request parameters over prose. They are enforced rather than merely requested:

```python theme={null}
tools=[{
    "type": "web_search",
    "filters": {
        "search_domain_filter": ["sec.gov"],
        "search_after_date_filter": "01/01/2026",
    },
}]
```

> [!TIP]
>
> Built-in tools like `web_search` and `fetch_url` generally work without much prompt-side coaching. Reach for `web_search` filters and `response_format` before adding more instruction prose — parameters are enforced directly and don't re-process on every loop step the way system-prompt tokens do.

## Read the sources back

A grounded answer comes with its evidence. Retrieval tools attach their results to the response `output` array (for example `search_results` items alongside the `message`), so you can surface citations or verify claims. See the per-tool reference pages — starting with [Web Search → Response shape](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/tools/web-search.md#response-shape) — for exact response shapes.

## Next steps

> [card] [Give it tools](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/building-agents/give-it-tools.md)
>
> Enable built-in tools and your own custom tools, then read their results.

> [card] [Prompt Guide](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/prompt-guide.md)
>
> Full prompting patterns and best practices.

Agent API tools overview
body:
# Tools overview

> The tools an Agent API run can call - Perplexity-hosted built-in tools, remote MCP servers, and your own custom functions - and where to go for each.

Tools are what turn a model into an agent.
On its own a model answers only from what it already knows; tools let it search the live web, fetch a page, run code, or call into your own systems.
You enable tools by listing them in the `tools` array, and within a single request the model runs an agentic loop — it reasons, calls a tool, observes the result, and repeats until it can answer.

## Four kinds of tools

| Kind | What it is | Where the model runs it |
| - | - | - |
| Built-in tools | Perplexity-hosted capabilities, enabled by `type`. | Inside the loop; Perplexity runs it and returns results inline. |
| [Connectors](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/tools/connectors.md) | Managed services or your own MCP server, configured once for a Project and selected with `type: connector` and `id`. | Inside the loop; calls run without approval by default. Use [approvals](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/tools/mcp.md#approvals) to review calls before they run. |
| [MCP servers](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/tools/mcp.md) | Your own remote MCP server, connected with `type: mcp`. | Inside the loop; calls run without approval by default. Use [approvals](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/tools/mcp.md#approvals) to review calls before they run. |
| [Custom functions](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/tools/custom-functions.md) | Functions you control, declared with a JSON Schema. | Paused back to you; you run the call and return the result. |

## Built-in tools

Enable each by its `type`. Every tool has its own reference page for full settings, response shape, and pricing.

| Tool | `type` | Use it to |
| - | - | - |

# OpenAI Compatibility

> Use existing OpenAI SDKs with Perplexity's Agent API and understand the compatibility differences.

## Overview

Perplexity's Agent API supports the OpenAI Responses API interface, so you can use existing OpenAI client libraries by changing the base URL and providing your Perplexity API key. The APIs are not identical, and some defaults and Perplexity extensions differ.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Endpoint Note:** Perplexity's canonical Agent API endpoint is `POST /v1/agent`. For OpenAI SDK compatibility, `POST /v1/responses` is also accepted as an alias — the OpenAI SDK automatically routes `client.responses.create()` to `/v1/responses`, which Perplexity handles seamlessly. No SDK changes are needed beyond setting the base URL.

One difference is the [MCP approval contract](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/tools/mcp.md#approvals): Agent API treats omitted or `null` `require_approval` as `"never"`, while OpenAI defaults MCP calls to approval.

> [!TIP]
>
> **We recommend using the [Perplexity SDK](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/sdk/overview.md)** for the best experience with full type safety, enhanced features, and effort level support. Use OpenAI SDKs if you're already integrated and need drop-in compatibility.

> )

>     model="openai/gpt-5.6-sol",

> )
>
> print(response.output_text)
> ```

# Search API Overview

> The Search API returns ranked web results as JSON, not a generated answer. What each result contains, the request controls and limits, the price per request, and when to use it instead of the Agent API.

## What you get

The Search API is one endpoint, `POST https://api.perplexity.ai/search`. You send a query and get back ranked web results as structured data for your own code to filter, store, or hand to a model. There is no generated answer and no token billing.

Each result has:

| Field | Contents |
| - | - |
| `title` | Title of the page |
| `url` | URL of the page |
| `snippet` | Query-relevant text extracted from the page, cut to `max_tokens_per_page`. Can be an empty string, so check it before you use the result. |
| `date` | Publication date, or `null` |
| `last_updated` | Date the page was last updated, or `null` |

The response also carries a request `id`. A `server_time` field is present and may be `null`.

```python Python theme={null}
from perplexity import Perplexity

client = Perplexity()

search = client.search.create(
    query="renewable energy technologies",
    max_results=10,
    max_tokens=50000,
    max_tokens_per_page=4096
)

for result in search.results:
    print(f"{result.title}: {result.url}")
```

```typescript TypeScript theme={null}
const search = await client.search.create({

    max_tokens: 50000,
    max_tokens_per_page: 4096
});

for (const result of search.results) {
    console.log(`${result.title}: ${result.url}`);
}
```

```json Response theme={null}
}
```

## Controls

| Parameter | What it does | Limits |
| - | - | - |
| `query` | One query, or an array of related queries processed independently | Up to 5 queries per request |
| `max_results` | Number of results to return | 1 to 20 for web search, up to 50 for people search; default 10 |
| `search_type` | `web` (default), `fast` for lower latency and lower cost, or `people` | See [Fast Search](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search/fast-search.md) and [People Search](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search/filters/people-search.md) |
| `max_tokens`, `max_tokens_per_page` | How much page content to extract, in total and per result | 1 to 1,000,000 tokens each |
| `search_domain_filter` | Include only, or exclude with a `-` prefix, specific domains | Up to 20 domains, one mode per request |
| `search_language_filter` | Restrict results to languages | Up to 20 ISO 639-1 codes |
| `search_recency_filter` | `hour`, `day`, `week`, `month`, or `year` | |
| `search_after_date_filter`, `search_before_date_filter`, `last_updated_after_filter`, `last_updated_before_filter` | Publication and update date windows | `MM/DD/YYYY` |
| `country` | Return results more relevant to a region | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code |

Full parameter reference: [POST /search](https://docs.perplexity.ai/api-reference/search-post.md). Agent API fields such as `model`, `effort`, `instructions`, and `tools` are not part of a search request.

## Use these results in your own agent

Everything your agent needs from a Search response is `title`, `url`, and `snippet`. Install the Perplexity Python library (`pip install perplexityai`, imported as `perplexity`) or the TypeScript SDK (`npm install @perplexity-ai/perplexity_ai`), set `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY` in the environment, and the client picks the key up. Then:

* Cap the text you hand the model with `max_tokens_per_page` (per result) and `max_tokens` (whole response). These change what comes back, not the price.
* Pass `query` as an array of up to five related queries to fan out in one request. Five is the limit, so check the length before you send. The request is billed once but uses one rate-limit unit per query. Each query is processed independently and the results come back in one `results` list. Dedupe by `url` before you hand them to the model.
* Skip results whose `snippet` is empty. Keep the `url` so the model can cite it.

```python Python theme={null}
from perplexity import Perplexity

client = Perplexity()

MAX_QUERIES = 5  # Search API limit per request

queries = ["US renewable energy tax credits 2026", "state renewable portfolio standards"]
if len(queries) > MAX_QUERIES:
    raise ValueError(f"Search accepts at most {MAX_QUERIES} queries per request, got {len(queries)}")

search = client.search.create(
    query=queries,
    max_results=5,
    max_tokens_per_page=1024,
    max_tokens=4000,
)

sources, seen_urls = [], set()
for r in search.results:
    snippet = r.snippet.strip()
    if not snippet or r.url in seen_urls:
        continue  # no extracted text, or a URL already kept
    seen_urls.add(r.url)
    sources.append({"title": r.title, "url": r.url, "snippet": snippet})

context = "\n\n".join(f"{s['title']} ({s['url']})\n{s['snippet']}" for s in sources)
print(context if sources else "No results with extracted text.")
```

```typescript Typescript theme={null}
import Perplexity from '@perplexity-ai/perplexity_ai';

const client = new Perplexity();

const MAX_QUERIES = 5; // Search API limit per request

const queries = ["US renewable energy tax credits 2026", "state renewable portfolio standards"];
if (queries.length > MAX_QUERIES) {
    throw new Error(`Search accepts at most ${MAX_QUERIES} queries per request, got ${queries.length}`);
}

const search = await client.search.create({
    query: queries,
    max_results: 5,
    max_tokens_per_page: 1024,
    max_tokens: 4000,
});

const seenUrls = new Set<string>();
const sources: { title: string; url: string; snippet: string }[] = [];
for (const r of search.results) {
    const snippet = r.snippet.trim();
    if (!snippet || seenUrls.has(r.url)) {
        continue; // no extracted text, or a URL already kept
    }
    seenUrls.add(r.url);
    sources.push({ title: r.title, url: r.url, snippet });
}

const context = sources.map((s) => `${s.title} (${s.url})\n${s.snippet}`).join("\n\n");
console.log(sources.length ? context : "No results with extracted text.");
```

```bash cURL theme={null}
curl -X POST https://api.perplexity.ai/search \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERPLEXITY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "query": ["US renewable energy tax credits 2026", "state renewable portfolio standards"],
    "max_results": 5,
    "max_tokens_per_page": 1024,
    "max_tokens": 4000
  }' | jq '[.results[] | select(.snippet | test("\\S"))]
          | reduce .[] as $r ([]; if any(.[]; .url == $r.url) then . else . + [$r] end)
          | map({title, url, snippet})'
```

Wrap that code in a tool the model can call. Each guide has the tool definition, the handler, and the tool-call loop:

* [OpenAI SDK](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search/agent-sdks/openai.md), [Anthropic SDK](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search/agent-sdks/anthropic.md), and [Gemini SDK](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search/agent-sdks/gemini.md): Search as a function tool in your own agent loop.
* [Perplexity API MCP server](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/integrations/mcp-server.md): the `perplexity_search` tool for Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, and other MCP clients, with no handler to write.
* [Perplexity CLI](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/cli/overview.md): `pplx search web` returns the same JSON from a shell, for coding agents that run commands.
* [Search SDK](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search-sdk/overview.md): a Python library that adds built-in concurrency, provenance, and checkpointing on top of the same Search results and page snippets.

## Price and rate limit

| Item | Detail |
| - | - |
| Web search | \$5.00 per 1,000 successful requests |
| Fast Search (`search_type: "fast"`) | \$1.00 per 1,000 successful requests |
| Billing unit | One successful `POST /search` request. A request with five queries is one billing unit. Invalid, rate-limited, and failed requests are not billed. No token charges. |
| Rate limit | 50 query units per second, same for every usage tier. Each query in a multi-query request counts as one unit. |

Details: [Search API pricing](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/pricing.md#search-api-pricing) and [Search API rate limits](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/admin/rate-limits-usage-tiers.md#search-api-rate-limits).

## Search API or Agent API

| You want | Use |
| - | - |
| Ranked results your code filters, stores, or feeds to your own model | Search API |
| A finished answer with citations, written by a model that searched for you | [Agent API](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/quickstart.md) with the `web_search` tool |
| Sources, not prose, returned to an agent you run on another provider | Search API as a function tool |
| Sources returned to an agent that already runs on the Agent API | The Agent API `web_search` tool |

## Extracted text, not page reading

`POST /search` takes queries, not URLs. Each result's `snippet` is text extracted from that page that is relevant to your query, cut to `max_tokens_per_page`. It is not the full page, and there is no parameter to re-fetch a page live or to control cache age. `search_recency_filter`, the date filters, and the `date` and `last_updated` fields on each result are how you select and check freshness.

To get text from URLs you already have:

* [Perplexity CLI](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/cli/overview.md#generate-query-relevant-snippets): `pplx content snippets "<query>" <url> [<url> ...]` returns query-relevant passages from up to 50 URLs you name, with total and per-page token budgets and failures reported per URL.
* [Search SDK](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search-sdk/overview.md): `pplx_srch_sdk.content.snippets(query=..., urls=[...])` does the same from Python, one result per URL, each with `text` or an `error`.
* [Agent API `fetch_url` tool](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/tools/fetch-url-content): a hosted model fetches and reads a URL during an Agent API run. It is a tool inside that run, billed with the run, not a standalone endpoint you call with a URL.

## Ways to call it

* [Quickstart](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search/quickstart.md) with the Perplexity Python library, the TypeScript SDK, and cURL
* [Perplexity CLI](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/cli/overview.md) for the same ranked results as JSON from a shell
* As a function tool in the [OpenAI](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search/agent-sdks/openai.md), [Anthropic](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search/agent-sdks/anthropic.md), and [Gemini](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search/agent-sdks/gemini.md) SDKs
* [Search SDK](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search-sdk/overview.md), a Python library for composing multi-step retrieval in code
* [Interactive Playground](https://console.perplexity.ai/project/playground/search), no API key required

# Fast Search

> Use search_type fast on the Search API for lower-latency, lower-cost web results.

## Overview

Fast Search reduces search latency and cost in agent workflows. Set `search_type: "fast"` on a Search API request, or on the `perplexity_search` tool in the [Perplexity MCP server](#use-fast-search-in-the-mcp-server).

The Search API charges \$1.00 per 1,000 Fast Search requests instead of \$5.00 for standard web search.

> [!NOTE]
>
> For Fast Search inside the Agent API, see [Web Search: Search Type](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/tools/web-search.md#search-type). Fast Search is a search type, not the Agent API `fast` effort level.

## When to use Fast Search

| Use | When |
| - | - |
| `search_type: "fast"` | Day-to-day agentic work: tool calls inside agent loops, high-volume retrieval, and latency-sensitive applications. |
| `search_type: "web"` (default) | Rare, difficult, or ambiguous questions. |

If you omit `search_type`, the request uses standard web search.

## Use Fast Search

Set `search_type` to `"fast"` on a `POST /search` request. Results use the same response format as standard web search.

First, [install a library and set `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY`](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search/quickstart#installation). Passing `search_type="fast"` requires Perplexity Python library 0.43.6 or later, or TypeScript SDK 0.38.6 or later. See [SDK support](#sdk-support).

```python Python theme={null}
from perplexity import Perplexity

client = Perplexity()

search = client.search.create(
    query="latest stable Rust release",
    search_type="fast",
    max_results=5
)

for result in search.results:
    print(f"{result.title}: {result.url}")
```

```typescript Typescript theme={null}
import Perplexity from '@perplexity-ai/perplexity_ai';

const client = new Perplexity();

const search = await client.search.create({
    query: "latest stable Rust release",
    search_type: "fast",
    max_results: 5
});

for (const result of search.results) {
    console.log(`${result.title}: ${result.url}`);
}
```

```bash cURL theme={null}
curl -X POST 'https://api.perplexity.ai/search' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERPLEXITY_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "query": "latest stable Rust release",
    "search_type": "fast",
    "max_results": 5
  }' | jq
```

Fast Search accepts `max_results` from 1 to 20. Values above 20 are only supported with `search_type: "people"`. See [People Search](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search/filters/people-search.md).

## SDK support

`search_type: "fast"` is a typed parameter in these library versions:

| Library | Minimum version | Upgrade |
| - | - | - |
| Perplexity Python library (`perplexityai`) | 0.43.6 | `pip install --upgrade perplexityai` |
| TypeScript SDK (`@perplexity-ai/perplexity_ai`) | 0.38.6 | `npm install @perplexity-ai/perplexity_ai@latest` |

Older versions reject `"fast"`. The Python library raises a validation error and the TypeScript SDK fails type checking. If you can't upgrade, pass `extra_body={"search_type": "fast"}` in Python or cast the value with `as any` in TypeScript.

## Use Fast Search in the MCP server

The `perplexity_search` tool in the [Perplexity MCP server](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/integrations/mcp-server.md) accepts an optional `search_type` argument, `"web"` or `"fast"`. The hosted server at `https://api.perplexity.ai/mcp` supports it, as does the local `@perplexity-ai/mcp-server` package from version 1.3.0.

The model in your MCP client chooses the argument when it calls the tool. The tool description tells it to prefer `"fast"` for routine lookups and keep `"web"` for rare or ambiguous questions. To request Fast Search explicitly, say so in your prompt, for example "Use fast search to find the latest stable Rust release." The tool call looks like this:

```json theme={null}
{
  "name": "perplexity_search",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "latest stable Rust release",
    "search_type": "fast",
    "max_results": 5
  }
}
```

If the client omits `search_type`, the tool uses standard web search.

## Pricing

| API | Standard (`web`) | Fast (`fast`) |
| - | :-: | :-: |
| Search API | \$5.00 per 1K requests | \$1.00 per 1K requests |

Search API billing counts each successful `POST /search` request, the same as standard web search. In the [API console](https://console.perplexity.ai), Fast Search requests appear as **Fast Search API Requests Count** under Search API usage.

There are no additional token-based charges. See [Pricing](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/pricing.md).

## Next Steps

> [card] [Search API Quickstart](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search/quickstart.md)
>
> Filters, multi-query search, and content controls

> [card] [API Reference](https://docs.perplexity.ai/api-reference/search-post.md)
>
> Full Search API parameters

> [card] [Pricing](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/pricing.md)
>
> Search and tool pricing

# Rate Limits & Usage Tiers

## What are Usage Tiers?

Usage tiers determine your **rate limits** and access to **beta features** based on your cumulative API spending. As you spend more on API credits over time, you automatically advance to higher tiers with increased rate limits. Higher tiers unlock higher request and token limits, and once you reach a tier, you keep it permanently with no downgrade.

> [!NOTE]
>
> You can check your current usage tier on the [Pricing page](https://console.perplexity.ai/project/pricing?tab=usage-tiers) in the API Console.

***

## Tier Progression

| Tier | Total Credits Purchased | Status |
| - | - | - |
| **Tier 0** | \$0 | New accounts, limited access |
| **Tier 1** | \$50+ | Light usage, basic limits |
| **Tier 2** | \$250+ | Regular usage |
| **Tier 3** | \$500+ | Heavy usage |
| **Tier 4** | \$1,000+ | Production usage |
| **Tier 5** | \$5,000+ | Enterprise usage |

> [!NOTE]
>
> Tiers are based on **cumulative purchases** across your account lifetime, not current balance.

***

## Orchestrator API Rate Limits

Orchestrator API requests are rate limited. When a request is rate limited, or an upstream model is overloaded, the API returns a `429` with a `Retry-After` header — retry after the indicated interval.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Requests rejected with a `429` are not billed.

***

## Agent API Rate Limits

Two kinds of limits apply to Agent API requests, and a request must pass both:

* **A request limit** (queries per second, QPS) for each API organization, shared across all models.
* **Token limits** (tokens per minute, TPM, and tokens per hour, TPH) for each API organization and model.

Both are shared across every API key in the organization. Because token limits are separate from the request limit, you can receive a `429` while your request rate is well under your QPS limit, once usage already recorded in the rolling window has reached the model's token budget. The size of the rejected request itself does not matter; the check looks only at usage already recorded.

**Which limit did you hit?** Read `error.type` in the `429` body:

| `error.type` | Meaning | What to do |
| - | - | - |
| `request_rate_limit_exceeded` | Request limit (QPS) | Wait `Retry-After` (normally 1 second), then retry |
| `token_rate_limit_exceeded` | Token limit; the message names the window (`TPM` or `TPH`) | Wait `Retry-After` seconds, then retry with backoff |
| `overloaded` | Not a rate limit. Upstream model capacity | Retry with backoff, or use the [`models` fallback list](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/model-fallback) |

A `429` response carries `Retry-After` but no `x-ratelimit-*` headers.

### Agent API Request Limits

Every Agent API call counts against one request limit shared across models and API keys in the organization: `POST /v1/agent`, `GET /v1/agent/{id}` polls, cancel, resume, and file downloads, on both the `/v1/agent` and `/v1/responses` paths. There is no separate per-model request limit. Polling is not free: at 1 QPS, polling once a second leaves no room for new requests. Poll with backoff or use streaming reconnect.

| Tier | QPS (Queries per Second) |
| :-: | :-: |
| **Tier 0** | 1 QPS |
| **Tier 1** | 3 QPS |
| **Tier 2** | 8 QPS |
| **Tier 3** | 17 QPS |
| **Tier 4** | 33 QPS |
| **Tier 5** | 33 QPS |

The limit uses a rolling one-second window. Each accepted request counts against the organization's shared Agent API request limit for one second, regardless of the model selected.

Successful responses include `x-ratelimit-limit`, `x-ratelimit-remaining`, `x-ratelimit-used`, and `x-ratelimit-reset` (Unix seconds) headers for the request limit. A `429` carries `Retry-After` instead, and no response reports token budget.

### Agent API Token Rate Limits

Token limits apply per organization and per model. Each model has its own budget, so traffic on one model does not use another model's budget. Both windows are rolling: TPM covers roughly the last minute and TPH covers roughly the last hour, and neither resets at the top of a minute or hour.

| Tier | TPM (Tokens per Minute) | TPH (Tokens per Hour) |
| :-: | :-: | :-: |
| **Tier 0** | 5,000,000 | 300,000,000 |
| **Tier 1** | 6,000,000 | 360,000,000 |
| **Tier 2** | 8,000,000 | 480,000,000 |
| **Tier 3** | 10,000,000 | 600,000,000 |
| **Tier 4** | 13,000,000 | 780,000,000 |
| **Tier 5** | 16,000,000 | 960,000,000 |

Token usage includes all input tokens (uncached, cached, and cache write) and all output tokens, including reasoning tokens. A request can make several model calls while it uses tools, including helper models used inside tools such as `fetch_url` content extraction and `sandbox`. All of them count toward the limit for the model you requested.

**Which model's budget:** if you set `models`, the budget is the first entry's; otherwise it is `model`'s. Tokens used by fallback models are charged to that budget. If you name only an effort level, usage counts against a budget keyed on the effort level name you send (an alias such as `pro-search` has a separate budget from `low`). If you name only a profile, the budget is the one for the profile's first model.

**Before a request starts:** if you are over a token limit, the API returns `429` and does not start the request. The `Retry-After` header gives the number of seconds to wait, and the message says which limit you hit:

```json theme={null}
{"error":{"message":"Token rate limit exceeded (TPM). Retry after the Retry-After interval.","type":"token_rate_limit_exceeded","code":429}}
```

Request limit errors use `request_rate_limit_exceeded` instead:

```json theme={null}
{"error":{"message":"Request rate limit exceeded, please try again later.","type":"request_rate_limit_exceeded","code":429}}
```

For token limits, `Retry-After` is the time until enough usage leaves the window, plus up to 10 seconds of random delay so that clients rejected together do not all retry at once. It is not a reservation: other requests in your organization can use the budget before your retry arrives. A request rejected for token budget still counts one request against the QPS limit, so tight retry loops on token `429`s can also trip the request limit.

**While a request runs:** tokens are not reserved when a request starts, so other requests in your organization can use up the limit. When that happens, the request pauses before its next turn and resumes automatically when tokens are available. A pause is not an error. Do not resubmit a paused request.

* **Streaming:** set `stream_options.include_token_pause_events: true` to receive `response.paused` and `response.resumed` events. These events do not end the stream, and keepalive comments are sent every 15 seconds while paused. They are off by default because some OpenAI SDKs treat unknown events as regular chunks. When you [reconnect](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/background-mode.md#stream-and-reconnect) with `GET /v1/agent/{id}?stream=true`, add `include_token_pause_events=true` to get them.
* **[Background](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/background-mode.md):** `GET /v1/agent/{id}` returns `status: "in_progress"` with a `paused` object. The object is removed when the request resumes or finishes.
* **Non-streaming:** the request cannot report a pause, so a pause appears only as added latency. The API holds the connection for at most 30 minutes, and a request your client abandons (timeout or disconnect) is cancelled server-side, even while it is paused. Use `background: true` for work that must survive a client timeout.

```text theme={null}
event: response.paused
data: {"type":"response.paused","reason":"token_rate_limit","window":"TPM","estimated_resume_in_seconds":12,"message":"Task paused: organization TPM budget exhausted. It will resume automatically; do not resubmit."}

event: response.resumed
data: {"type":"response.resumed"}
```

```json theme={null}
{"status":"in_progress","paused":{"reason":"token_rate_limit","window":"TPM","estimated_resume_at":1791302400}}
```

`window` is `TPM` or `TPH`. `estimated_resume_in_seconds` and `estimated_resume_at` (Unix time in seconds) are estimates, and `estimated_resume_at` can briefly be in the past while the request waits to resume. If `paused` is missing from a polled response, keep polling; that alone does not mean the request has resumed. Pause events have no `sequence_number`, so do not use them as `starting_after` values.

> [!TIP]
>
> **Handling token limits:**
>
> * Set client timeouts long enough to allow for pauses.
> * On a `429`, wait at least `Retry-After` seconds, then retry with exponential backoff and jitter.
> * Limit concurrent retries so they do not use up the limit again.
> * A foreground request that times out or disconnects is cancelled, not resumed, and the tokens it used still count. If a run must outlive client timeouts, submit it with `background: true` and poll.

***

## Search API Rate Limits

The Search API has separate rate limits that apply to all usage tiers:

| Endpoint | Rate Limit | Burst Capacity |
| - | - | - |
| POST `/search` | 50 query units per second | 50 query units |

**Search Rate Limiter Behavior:**

* **Single-query request**: Consumes 1 query unit
* **Multi-query request**: Consumes 1 query unit for each query in the array
* **Burst**: Can consume 50 query units instantly
* **Sustained**: 50 query units per second on average

> [!NOTE]
>
> Billing and rate limiting use different units. A successful request containing five queries is one billable Search API request, but it consumes five rate-limit units. Search rate limits are independent of your usage tier and apply consistently across all accounts using the same leaky bucket algorithm. See [Search API pricing](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/pricing.md#search-api-pricing) for billing details.

***

## Embeddings API Rate Limits

The Embeddings API uses tier-based rate limits that scale with your usage tier. Limits are higher than other APIs because each request is a single forward pass on an elastic backend.

| Tier | QPS (Queries per Second) |
| :-: | :-: |
| **Tier 0** | 85 QPS |
| **Tiers 1–3** | 170 QPS |
| **Tiers 4–5** | 335 QPS |

### Contextualized Embeddings

Contextualized embeddings have separate, higher limits (5× the standard embeddings tiers):

| Tier | Chunks per second |
| :-: | :-: |
| **Tier 0** | 415 chunks/s |
| **Tiers 1–3** | 835 chunks/s |
| **Tiers 4–5** | 1,670 chunks/s |

> [!NOTE]
>
> Contextualized embeddings are rate limited by **total chunks**, not by request count. The 16,000-chunk request limit is a structural ceiling. With an otherwise empty rate-limit window, the effective maximum is the lower of 16,000 chunks and your organization's one-second chunk allowance. Earlier requests in the window reduce the number of chunks currently available.

***

## How Rate Limiting Works

Rate limiter behavior differs by API; one algorithm does not apply across the platform. Refer to each API section above for the applicable limits.

### Agent API Rolling Window

Agent API requests use a rolling one-second window rather than continuous token refill. When the window is empty, requests can arrive together up to your tier's QPS limit. Additional requests are rejected until earlier requests become more than one second old and leave the window.

For example, an organization with a 33 QPS limit can make up to 33 Agent API requests in any rolling one-second period.

Agent API token limits also use rolling windows, so capacity returns gradually as older usage leaves the window instead of all at once on a clock boundary.

***

## What Happens When You Hit Rate Limits?

When you exceed your rate limits:

1. **429 Error** - Your request gets rejected with "Too Many Requests"
2. **Recovery Timing** - Capacity returns according to the applicable API's limiter. For the Agent API request limit, each accepted request leaves the rolling window after one second. For Agent API token limits, wait at least the `Retry-After` interval.
3. **Token Limits** - Agent API token limit errors use the type `token_rate_limit_exceeded` and include a `Retry-After` header. See [Agent API Token Rate Limits](#agent-api-token-rate-limits).

> [!TIP]
>
> **Best Practices:**
>
> * Monitor your usage to predict when you'll need higher tiers
> * Consider upgrading your tier proactively for production applications
> * Implement exponential backoff with jitter in your code
> * Pace Agent API traffic to stay within your tier's rolling one-second request limit and per-model token limits

***

## Upgrading Your Tier

**1. Check Current Tier**
